## Project Proposal for prompts.chat

Below is the completed proposal following the AAIF project proposal template. You can paste this directly into the issue form at `aaif/project-proposals`.

---

### Project Name

prompts.chat

### Project Description

prompts.chat (formerly Awesome ChatGPT Prompts) is the world's largest open-source prompt library for AI. It started in December 2022 as a simple curated list of ChatGPT prompts on GitHub and quickly became one of the most-starred repositories on the platform, reaching over 143,000 stars. Over time it evolved from a static Markdown file into a full social platform where users can share, discover, organize, and collect prompts that work across all major AI models (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Mistral, and others).

The project is built with Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, and Prisma. It supports 17 locales, AI-powered semantic search, an MCP server for tool integration, a CLI, a Chrome extension, and an iOS app. It can also be self-hosted as a white-label prompt library with custom branding, themes, and authentication providers.

prompts.chat has been featured in Forbes, referenced by Harvard and Columbia universities, cited in 40+ academic papers, and recognized as a GitHub Staff Pick. Its Hugging Face dataset is the most-liked dataset on the platform.

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

prompts.chat directly supports the mission of making agentic AI more accessible and practical for everyone. It serves as foundational infrastructure for AI interaction by:

- Providing open, community-curated prompt templates that help people get better results from AI agents and assistants.
- Offering an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server and API, which means any agentic AI tool can pull from the prompt library programmatically, making it a building block for agent workflows.
- Publishing all prompt data under CC0 (public domain), so anyone -- researchers, developers, companies -- can use, remix, and build on the content without restrictions.
- Maintaining a self-hostable platform that lets organizations run their own internal prompt libraries, directly supporting enterprise adoption of agentic AI practices.

The project bridges the gap between everyday users and AI systems. Better prompts lead to more effective AI agents, and an open library of high-quality prompts lowers the barrier for everyone.

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

prompts.chat is complementary to other AAIF projects focused on AI tooling and interoperability. While many foundation projects focus on model infrastructure, runtimes, or agent frameworks, prompts.chat addresses the human-AI interface layer. It provides the content and context that feed into those systems.

Its MCP server integration means it can plug directly into agentic AI toolchains that other AAIF projects may define or standardize. If there are projects working on agent orchestration or prompt management standards, prompts.chat would be a natural reference implementation and data source.

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

**Use cases:**
- Individual users browse and apply prompt templates to get better outputs from AI assistants for writing, coding, learning, and creative work.
- Development teams self-host the platform as an internal prompt library, sharing tested prompts across their organization.
- AI tool developers integrate the MCP server or API to provide prompt suggestions inside their products.
- Educators and researchers use prompts as teaching material for prompt engineering courses. Harvard and Columbia have referenced the project in their AI curriculum resources.
- The Hugging Face dataset is used by ML practitioners for fine-tuning, evaluation, and research.

**Evidence of adoption:**
- 143,000+ GitHub stars with 946 unique contributors and nearly 6,000 commits.
- Featured in Forbes, referenced by Harvard University and Columbia University.
- 40+ academic citations on Google Scholar.
- Most-liked dataset on Hugging Face.
- GitHub Staff Pick.
- Recognized by OpenAI co-founders Greg Brockman and Wojciech Zaremba, Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue, and former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke.
- Active sponsorship from multiple companies including Cognition (Windsurf), CodeRabbit, Sentry, and others.
- Published Chrome extension and iOS app.
- Docker images published to GitHub Container Registry, used by self-hosting organizations.

### Technical Committee Sponsor (if identified)

Not yet identified.

### GitHub Repository URL

https://github.com/f/prompts.chat

### License

CC0 1.0 Universal (Public Domain Dedication)

### Governance Model

The project currently follows a Benevolent Dictator For Life (BDFL) model led by the original creator, Fatih Kadir Akin (@f). Key decisions about architecture, features, and direction are made by the maintainer with input from community contributors through GitHub issues and pull requests.

Community members contribute prompts through the web platform (prompts.chat), which automatically syncs to the repository. Code contributions follow a standard fork-and-PR workflow with review by the core maintainer.

The project is open to transitioning to a more formal governance structure (such as LF Minimum Viable Governance) as part of joining the AAIF, including establishing a formal steering committee and documented decision-making processes.

### CI/CD & Release Workflow

The project uses GitHub Actions for continuous integration and delivery:

- **CI Pipeline (ci.yml):** Runs on every push to `main` and on pull requests. Sets up Node.js 24, installs dependencies, runs ESLint, and executes the Vitest test suite.
- **Docker Publish (docker-publish.yml):** Triggered on pushes to `main` and version tags. Runs the test suite first, then builds multi-architecture Docker images (amd64/arm64) and publishes them to GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io`).
- **Additional workflows:** Automated contributor list updates, scheduled credit resets, and spam detection.
- **Release cadence:** The project ships continuously. Changes to `main` trigger Docker image builds automatically. The npm package (`prompts.chat`) is published separately for CLI and self-hosting use.

### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

The contribution process is documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md` in the repository root. There are two main paths:

1. **Prompt contributions:** Users sign in at prompts.chat with their GitHub account, create prompts through the web interface, and submissions are automatically synced to the repository. Contributors are credited by their GitHub username.
2. **Code contributions:** For bug fixes, features, and documentation changes, contributors fork the repository, create a feature branch, and submit a pull request with a descriptive explanation. PRs are reviewed by the core maintainer before merging.

Prompt guidelines require that all prompts are tested, clearly titled, original, and appropriate for all audiences.

### Publicly Accessible Issue Tracker

https://github.com/f/prompts.chat/issues

### External Project Dependencies

Key runtime dependencies and their licenses:

| Dependency | License |
|---|---|
| Next.js 16 | MIT |
| React 19 | MIT |
| Prisma ORM 6 | Apache 2.0 |
| NextAuth.js 5 | ISC |
| next-intl | MIT |
| Radix UI | MIT |
| Tailwind CSS 4 | MIT |
| Zod | MIT |
| OpenAI SDK | Apache 2.0 |
| Lucide React | ISC |
| sharp | Apache 2.0 |
| bcryptjs | MIT |
| D3 | ISC |
| MCP SDK (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk) | MIT |

All dependencies use permissive open-source licenses.

### Maintainers & Contributors

**Core maintainer:**
- Fatih Kadir Akin (@f) - Creator and lead maintainer

**Active contributors (among many):**
- @devisasari - Significant prompt contributions
- @giorgiop - Significant prompt contributions
- @sinansonmez - Active contributor
- @wkaandemir - Active contributor
- @ersinkoc - Active contributor
- @senoldak - Active contributor

The project has 946 unique contributors in total. The contributor list is automatically maintained and visible at https://github.com/f/prompts.chat/graphs/contributors.

*Note:* The project's contributor base is largely individual community members rather than organization-affiliated developers. The maintainer is open to growing the core maintainer team as part of the foundation onboarding process.

### Leadership Team & Decision Process

**Current leadership:**
- Fatih Kadir Akin (@f) - Project lead, final decision-maker on all architectural, feature, and community matters.

**Decision process:**
- Feature requests and bug reports are discussed through GitHub issues.
- Pull requests are reviewed and merged by the project lead.
- Community feedback on prompts is gathered through the web platform's voting and comment system.
- Sponsorship and partnership decisions are made by the project lead.

The project is open to establishing a Technical Steering Committee and adopting a more distributed governance model as part of AAIF membership.

### Roadmap

Over the next 12 months:

1. **Prompt quality and curation** - Build out community moderation tools, prompt rating systems, and automated quality scoring to keep the library high-quality as it scales.
2. **Agent integration** - Expand MCP server capabilities, add support for agent-specific prompt formats, and build deeper integrations with popular AI agent frameworks.
3. **API and developer experience** - Formalize the public API, add API key management for third-party developers, and publish OpenAPI documentation.
4. **Internationalization** - Grow the current 17 locales, improve translation coverage, and add community-driven translation workflows.
5. **Self-hosting improvements** - Improve the white-label experience with better theming, plugin architecture for custom auth providers and storage backends, and streamlined Docker/Kubernetes deployment.
6. **Governance and community** - Establish a formal governance structure, grow the core maintainer team, and create a contributor ladder.
7. **Educational content** - Expand the interactive prompting book and the "Prompting for Kids" module with more chapters and languages.

### Security

The project has not yet applied for an OpenSSF Best Practices badge. This is something we plan to pursue as part of joining the AAIF. The project does follow several security best practices:

- Dependencies are kept up to date.
- Secrets are managed through environment variables and never committed to the repository.
- Authentication uses NextAuth.js with support for OAuth providers (GitHub, Google, Apple).
- Passwords (when using credentials auth) are hashed with bcrypt.
- The CI pipeline runs linting and tests on every PR.

### Website URL

https://prompts.chat

### Documented Governance Practices (if any)

No formal GOVERNANCE.md exists yet. The project follows the contribution guidelines documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. Establishing formal governance documentation is planned as part of the AAIF onboarding process.

### Links to Social Media Accounts

- GitHub: https://github.com/f/prompts.chat
- Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/datasets/fka/prompts.chat
- Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/promptschat/eemdohkhbaifiocagjlhibfbhamlbeej
- iOS App Store: https://apps.apple.com/tr/app/prompts-chat/id6756895736

### Details of Existing Financial Sponsorship

The project receives financial sponsorship through GitHub Sponsors and direct partnerships. Current sponsors include:

- Clemta
- Wiro.ai
- Cognition (Windsurf)
- CodeRabbit
- Sentry
- Each Labs
- CommandCode

Sponsorship is used to fund hosting, development time, and infrastructure costs.

### Infrastructure Needs or Requests

No immediate infrastructure needs. The project currently runs on Vercel for the web platform and uses GitHub Container Registry for Docker images. If the AAIF could provide:

- Shared CI/CD resources for expanded testing (cross-browser, performance)
- Support with OpenSSF Best Practices badge application
- Guidance on transitioning to a multi-maintainer governance model

These would be helpful but are not blockers.

### Additional Information

prompts.chat was one of the very first prompt libraries when it launched in December 2022, just days after ChatGPT's public release. It grew organically through community contributions and became a reference point for how people interact with AI models. The transition from a static Markdown list to a full-featured social platform reflects the project's commitment to evolving with the AI ecosystem.

The project's CC0 license makes it uniquely open. All prompt content is public domain, which means there are no licensing barriers for anyone to build on top of it. This aligns well with a foundation model where broad adoption and reuse are key goals.

We believe prompts.chat can serve as the community's shared prompt infrastructure under the AAIF, much like how package registries serve the software development community.

Good question. Let me walk through how prompts.chat maps against the lifecycle policy's actual acceptance criteria. There are some strong fits and a few real gaps.

---

## Stage Assessment

**Impact Stage is a stretch right now.** The project has massive adoption, but Impact requires multiple maintainers from multiple organizations, a formal governance process, and documented OWNERS.md/GOVERNANCE.md files. prompts.chat is essentially a single-maintainer project today.

**Growth Stage is the realistic target**, and the project is a strong candidate, but there are things to fix first.

---

## Mandatory Proposal Requirements -- Where You Stand

| Requirement | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Project name, description, mission alignment | Good | Covered well in the proposal |
| Relation to existing AAIF projects | Good | MCP integration angle is solid |
| Use cases and evidence of adoption | Very strong | 143k stars, Forbes, Harvard, Hugging Face, etc. |
| TC Sponsor | **Missing** | Required for Growth stage, not just optional |
| OSI-approved permissive license | **Problem** | CC0 1.0 is not an OSI-approved license (see below) |
| Public repository | Good | github.com/f/prompts.chat |
| Automated validation/delivery + release processes | Good | CI pipeline + Docker publish workflow |
| Public contribution process | Good | CONTRIBUTING.md exists |
| Public issue tracker | Good | GitHub Issues |
| External dependencies with licenses | Good | All permissive (MIT, Apache 2.0, ISC) |
| Core maintainers | Thin | Only one core maintainer listed |
| Leadership team and decision process | Described | BDFL model, honest about it |
| Documented governance (GOVERNANCE.md) | **Missing** | No formal governance doc |
| Official communication channels | **Missing from proposal** | No Discord, Slack, or mailing list mentioned |
| Website, social media, sponsorship | Good | All covered |

---

## Growth Stage Criteria -- Specific Gaps

The policy lists these acceptance criteria for Growth:

1. **"TC sponsor to champion the project and provide mentorship"** -- You don't have one yet. This is a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have. You will need to identify and secure a sponsor before or during the application.

2. **"Presentation of a growth plan to demonstrate diverse maintainership"** -- This is the biggest structural gap. The project has 946 contributors, but effectively one person with commit access. The growth plan needs to specifically lay out how you will bring in maintainers from other organizations.

3. **"Document that it is being used successfully in production at wide scale"** -- This one you crush. No issues here.

4. **"Demonstrate an appropriate ongoing flow of commits and merged contributions"** -- Nearly 6,000 commits, frequent activity. No issues.

5. **"Demonstrate that the current level of community participation is sufficient to meet the goals outlined in the growth plan"** -- This depends on how the growth plan is written. The community is very active on the prompt contribution side, but thin on the code/platform side.

---

## The License Issue

This is the most important thing to address. The policy says:

> "name of the OSI-approved permissive license under which the project is released"

CC0 1.0 Universal is **not** an OSI-approved license. OSI has explicitly declined to approve it. It is a Creative Commons public domain dedication, and while it is extremely permissive (more so than any OSI license), it does not appear on OSI's approved list.

You have a few options:

- **Dual-license the code** under an OSI-approved license (like MIT or Apache 2.0) while keeping CC0 for the prompt content/data. This is actually a common and natural split -- the application code under MIT, the prompt dataset under CC0.
- **Relicense entirely** under Apache 2.0 or MIT. Feasible since CC0 places no restrictions, but a bigger change.
- **Ask the TC** whether CC0 is acceptable given it is strictly more permissive than any OSI license. They might grant an exception, but the policy language is pretty clear.

The dual-license approach is probably the cleanest path and would actually make the project more attractive to enterprise adopters.

---

## What the Proposal Should Add or Change

1. **Desired stage:** Explicitly state "Growth" as the desired stage. The proposal I drafted didn't include this (it's optional per the template but the lifecycle policy says projects "should state their preferred lifecycle stage").

2. **Growth plan for diverse maintainership:** Add a concrete section about how you plan to grow from a single maintainer to a multi-org team. Name specific steps like creating a GOVERNANCE.md, defining a contributor ladder, granting commit access to active contributors, etc.

3. **License clarification:** Address the CC0/OSI issue head-on. Propose dual licensing or explain why CC0 should be accepted.

4. **Communication channels:** List any existing channels (GitHub Discussions, etc.) or state plans to create them.

5. **TC Sponsor:** Even if you don't have one yet, mention that you are actively seeking one. Better yet, reach out to TC members before submitting.

6. **GOVERNANCE.md and OWNERS.md:** The policy references these explicitly for Impact, and having drafts ready signals seriousness even for Growth.

---

## Bottom Line

The project's adoption, community size, and real-world impact are far beyond what most Growth stage applicants would have. The gaps are all on the governance and organizational maturity side -- single maintainer, no formal governance docs, no TC sponsor, and a license that doesn't technically meet the stated requirement. These are all fixable, and the project would be a very compelling Growth stage candidate once they are addressed. The license question is the one to sort out first since it may require actual changes to the repository.

# Governance

This document describes the governance model for prompts.chat.

## Overview

prompts.chat is an open-source project that welcomes contributions from anyone. The project operates with a small group of maintainers who are responsible for the overall direction, code review, and release process. We aim to grow this group over time and welcome new maintainers who demonstrate sustained, quality contributions.

## Roles

### Users

Anyone who uses prompts.chat, whether by browsing the website, self-hosting the platform, using the CLI, or integrating with the MCP server. Users are encouraged to file issues, suggest features, and contribute prompts.

### Contributors

Anyone who contributes to the project. This includes submitting prompts through the web platform, opening pull requests, reporting bugs, improving documentation, or helping other users. All contributors are listed at https://github.com/f/prompts.chat/graphs/contributors.

### Maintainers

People with commit access to the repository. Maintainers review and merge pull requests, triage issues, and participate in project decisions. The current list of maintainers is in [OWNERS.md](OWNERS.md).

Maintainers are expected to:
- Review pull requests in a timely manner
- Help triage and respond to issues
- Follow the project's code of conduct
- Participate in governance discussions when they arise

### Project Lead

The project lead has final decision-making authority on project direction, releases, and governance changes. The project lead is responsible for ensuring the project stays aligned with its mission and the broader community's needs.

## Becoming a Maintainer

New maintainers are added based on sustained, high-quality contributions and demonstrated understanding of the project. There is no fixed checklist, but the following signals are considered:

- A track record of accepted pull requests over several months
- Thoughtful code reviews on other people's contributions
- Constructive participation in issue discussions
- Reliability and follow-through on commitments

Any existing maintainer can nominate a contributor for maintainer status. The nomination is discussed among the current maintainers, and the project lead makes the final decision. We are actively looking to grow the maintainer team, especially from contributors at different organizations.

## Decision Making

Most day-to-day decisions (bug fixes, small features, documentation updates) are made through the standard pull request review process. Any maintainer can approve and merge a PR.

For larger decisions (new features with broad impact, architectural changes, governance changes, dependency additions), we use a "lazy consensus" approach:

1. A proposal is opened as a GitHub issue or discussion.
2. The proposal is left open for at least 7 days to allow feedback.
3. If there are no objections from maintainers, the proposal is accepted.
4. If there are objections, the maintainers discuss and try to reach agreement. The project lead has final say if consensus cannot be reached.

## Changing This Document

Changes to this governance document follow the same decision-making process described above. Any maintainer or contributor can propose changes by opening a pull request.

## Code of Conduct

All participants in the project are expected to be respectful, constructive, and welcoming. We do not tolerate harassment, discrimination, or abusive behavior in any form. Violations can be reported to the project lead or through the channels listed in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

# Owners

This file lists the current maintainers and emeritus maintainers of prompts.chat.

## Project Lead

| Name | GitHub | Affiliation |
|------|--------|-------------|
| Fatih Kadir Akin | [@f](https://github.com/f) | Independent |

## Maintainers

| Name | GitHub | Affiliation | Since |
|------|--------|-------------|-------|
| Fatih Kadir Akin | [@f](https://github.com/f) | Independent | Dec 2022 |

## Emeritus Maintainers

None yet.

---

We are actively looking to grow the maintainer team. If you are interested in becoming a maintainer, please see [GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md) for how the process works. Sustained contributions and involvement in code review are the best way to get started.
